q: The notion of computational universality in cellular automata (e.g., Rule 110) relates to dynamical systems because:
opts: A CA that can simulate any Turing machine must exhibit complex dynamics (not periodic or eventually periodic)
Universal CAs are always chaotic in the topological sense
exp: Computational universality implies undecidability of the halting problem for configurations, which requires complex (non-periodic, non-quiescent) orbits. Rule 110's universality (proven by Cook) makes many properties of its dynamics undecidable.
